title: Trancy201 — approximate factory recreation
method: Source-only spectrograms show a stable low pair around 87/131 Hz (F2/C3), changing to 104/156 Hz (Ab2/Eb3), then 69/104 Hz (C#2/Ab2), while bright detuned peaks move independently in a higher melody. This reconstruction interprets the low pair as one played root plus an oscillator fifth and transcribes the upper melody separately. This is a plausible split-keyboard arrangement, not a unique recovery of the original playing or patch structure.
uncertainties: ESTIMATED MIDI: original performance MIDI is unavailable. Notes, onsets, note-offs and overlaps are interpretations of the source MP3, not recovered original events.
Velocity 100 is an explicit constant placeholder, not an estimate of the original key velocities. Note-off velocity is 64. No original controller or pedal events have been recovered.
The factory parameter dump is unavailable. The companion patch is a newly authored approximate recreation, not exact factory SysEx; an exported SysEx file encodes this approximation only.

Audio frequencies do not uniquely reveal played key numbers: original oscillator tuning, octave switches and system transpose are unknown. The MIDI and companion patch jointly choose an octave interpretation.

Times are measured from decoded source MP3 audio; encoder delay, hardware response latency and prior effect state are not removed. Timing is approximate, generally 20–40 ms; short transitions can be less certain.
LOWER CONFIDENCE: layered and detuned source audio makes note-versus-harmonic and chord-versus-oscillator interval interpretation ambiguous.
The original may use DUAL mode, played chords, a built-in phrase, or another allocation. SPLIT mode and the lower oscillator fifth are an authored arrangement to reproduce the main spectral parts.
Bright peaks around 700 Hz may include strong second harmonics of a lower lead. The chosen high melody can therefore differ by an octave from the original played notes.
Short melody transitions and gates are coarse estimates; no original arpeggio pattern or rhythm MIDI was available.

patch_design.name: APX Trancy
rationale: The low spectral families support a fifth-separated bass layer. A split patch allows its root progression to move independently of the upper lead.
Broad clusters around the upper notes support a detuned supersaw timbre; the lead uses two moderate-spread supersaws.
Short upper release and a small reverb approximate the residual tone after the repeated gated phrases.

Preview spectrum made the bass layer dominate and the upper line too narrow. Increased upper level/spread and reduced lower level make the two parts closer to the relative strength and detuning visible in the source.
uncertainties: All voicing values are authored approximation parameters, not measured or recovered Roland factory parameter values.
